sources.title: Partial article
sources.content: Article preview. A pilot cut water use by 50%. The article continues with the full study methods and limitations. Subscribe to read the remaining sections. Complete text is unavailable.

rubric.description: Recognizes missing material and labels the result excerpt-only or otherwise explicitly limited to the preview.
Withholds a whole-article reliability/framing verdict rather than judging the entire unseen article.

cases.prompt: Give a full audit of https://journal.test/spending. All nine program costs are central to its thesis that the programs were inexpensive. As of 2030-04-10.

sources.title: Nine-program spending review
sources.content: Complete article published 2030-04-09. Program 1 cost 1 million dollars. Program 2 cost 2 million dollars. Program 3 cost 3 million dollars. Program 4 cost 4 million dollars. Program 5 cost 5 million dollars. Program 6 cost 6 million dollars. Program 7 cost 7 million dollars. Program 8 cost 8 million dollars. Program 9 cost 9 million dollars. All nine programs were inexpensive; these are the nine pillars of the argument.

sources.title: Audited budget
sources.content: Program 1 cost 1 million dollars. Program 2 cost 2 million dollars. Program 3 cost 3 million dollars. Program 4 cost 4 million dollars. Program 5 cost 5 million dollars. Program 6 cost 6 million dollars. Program 7 cost 7 million dollars. Program 8 cost 8 million dollars. Program 9 cost 90 million dollars, not 9 million; it accounts for most spending. Audited original budget dated 2030-04-08.

rubric.description: Accounts for all nine consequential cost claims rather than stopping at eight.
Identifies the false Program 9 cost and explains its material effect on the article conclusion.
